subject: zoology_2
question_text: Write a short note on Neo-Darwinism.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.41, SAQ 39. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Revised 2026-09-05 after the examiner audit: the gene mutation line now says a change in DNA can alter the phenotype, because a change in DNA does not always alter it, and the matching common mistake was reworded.

steps.label: The two kinds of mutation
steps.why: Darwin knew variation existed but not where it came from; Neo-Darwinism names mutation as the source.
common_mistakes: Naming only one kind of mutation. Gene and chromosomal are separate factors.
Leaving out that gene mutations are the source of new variations.
steps.memory_tip: Gene mutation changes a letter; chromosomal mutation moves a whole block.
steps.margin_note: Name all five factors, then take them in turn.

steps.label: Genetic recombination
steps.why: Crossing over reshuffles existing genes into new combinations, so variation appears without any new mutation.
common_mistakes: Placing recombination in mitosis. It happens during meiosis.
Saying recombination creates new genes. It creates new combinations.
steps.memory_tip: Recombination deals the same cards in a new order.
steps.margin_note: Two lines are enough for this factor.
lines: an exchange of chromosomal bits and genes

steps.label: Natural selection
steps.why: Mutation and recombination only supply the variation; selection decides which of it survives.
common_mistakes: Saying natural selection creates variation. It only sorts it.
Leaving out that the selected variations continue in later generations.
steps.margin_note: One line for the fourth factor.

steps.label: Reproductive isolation
steps.why: Two groups that cannot interbreed stop sharing genes, so they drift apart until they are separate species.
common_mistakes: Confusing reproductive isolation with geographical distance alone.
Leaving out the outcome: new species.
steps.memory_tip: No interbreeding means no shared genes, and in time two species.
steps.margin_note: End with the formation of species.
